newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL tin dips slightly on ringgit uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: KL tin dips slightly on ringgit uncertainty.

text.p: Malaysia's spot tin price fell six cents to 14.59 ringgit ($5.26) a kg on Monday due to uncertainties over the ringgit and an overnight fall on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
"I think they (the players) decided to sell because the ringgit strengthened a little this morning, and also the LME was down on Friday," said a trader.
"But the market is still strong and should go up again if the ringgit weakens," he said.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7680 to a dollar in Kuala Lumpur prior to the opening of the tin market.
The currency, however, slid to 2.7745 by 0400 GMT when the tin market closed.
At Friday's opening, there were buyers for 87 tonnes and sellers for 101 tonnes. Final turnover was 102 tonnes, against 134 on Friday, and was absorbed by Japanese, European and local interests.
The closing price was at a premium of $30 against the LME, compared to a discount of $15 on Friday, traders said.
